questions.question: Amir is managing a project to build a mobile banking app for Lakeshore Credit Union, which has promised its 30,000 members that the app will launch on June 1. His team is two weeks behind schedule. His boss suggests skipping the final security testing to make the date, noting that the credit union's last app had no problems. What is the most ethical response?

options.A: Launch quietly and fix problems later
options.B: Explain the risks and propose a new date
options.C: Skip the testing as his boss suggests
options.D: Report the project as finished early

questions.explanation: Explain the risks and propose a new date. Skipping security testing on a financial app could expose members' personal and account information to criminals. Amir should explain the risks to his boss and propose a realistic launch date or other ways to save time without cutting security. Skipping testing or launching quietly puts users at risk, and reporting the project as finished when it isn't is dishonest. Ethical project managers protect the people their projects affect, even when that means difficult conversations with leaders.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the role of ethics in project management

questions.question: A new hire notices that projects backed by a well-liked senior manager get approved faster than others, even when they aren't stronger. This is an example of

options.B: company pricing policy.
options.C: formal job descriptions.

questions.explanation: Office politics. Office politics involves how people use relationships, influence and informal power to get things done or gain advantages at work. It can be positive, such as building alliances to support a good idea, or negative, such as gossip and manipulation. It isn't the same as formal job descriptions, pricing policy or safety rules, which are official parts of how a business runs. Understanding office politics helps employees navigate workplace relationships, build support for their ideas and avoid being drawn into harmful behavior. Positive office politics can help good ideas gain support.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of office politics

questions.question: An employee faces an ethical dilemma when

options.A: the law clearly requires one action.
options.B: each option rests on important values.
options.C: there is only one obvious correct choice.
options.D: a decision has no effect on anyone.

questions.explanation: Each option rests on important values. An ethical dilemma is a situation in which a person must choose between options that involve competing values, such as loyalty to a coworker and honesty to an employer. Each choice seems to have something right about it, which makes the decision difficult. When there is only one obvious correct choice, a decision affects no one or the law clearly requires an action, there isn't a true dilemma. Recognizing dilemmas helps employees slow down and think carefully before acting.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain reasons for ethical dilemmas

questions.question: An ethical project manager who realizes a project will miss its deadline should

options.A: cut safety steps to finish faster.
options.B: blame the client for the delay.
options.C: hide the delay until the last day.

questions.explanation: Tell stakeholders honestly and early. Ethics in project management include honesty with stakeholders, fairness to team members and protecting safety and quality. Telling stakeholders about a delay early gives them time to adjust plans and keeps their trust. Hiding the delay until the last day can cause bigger problems, blaming the client without cause is dishonest, and cutting safety steps puts people at risk. Project managers often face pressure to look successful, which is why ethical guidelines encourage transparent reporting of problems.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the role of ethics in project management

questions.question: A store manager has authority over schedules, discounts and refunds. She shows that she knows how to use power appropriately by

options.B: making decisions for personal gain.
options.C: threatening employees who disagree.

questions.explanation: Using authority fairly. Appropriate use of power means using authority fairly and responsibly to reach goals and support others, such as assigning tasks based on skills and listening to employees' input. Giving favors to friends, threatening those who disagree and making decisions for personal gain all misuse power, which damages trust and morale and can create legal problems. Leaders who use power well explain their decisions, treat people consistently and admit when they make mistakes. Employees are more likely to follow leaders they see as fair.

performanceIndicator.text: Use power appropriately

questions.question: Priya, a newly promoted shift lead at a movie theater, now decides who works the busy Friday and Saturday night shifts. Which action shows she is using her power appropriately?

options.B: Assigning extra weekends to anyone who disagrees
options.C: Giving weekends off only to her friends
options.D: Rotating weekend shifts fairly among staff

questions.explanation: Rotating weekend shifts fairly among staff. Rotating weekend shifts fairly treats all employees equally and shows that Priya uses her authority to benefit the team, not herself or her friends. Giving friends weekends off is favoritism, assigning extra weekends to people who disagree is retaliation, and taking every weekend off herself puts her personal interests first. New leaders are watched closely by their former peers, so fair, consistent decisions early on build trust. Using power fairly makes employees more likely to support a supervisor's decisions. Explaining how shifts are assigned helps employees accept the schedule.

performanceIndicator.text: Use power appropriately

questions.question: Simone gets a text alert that $185 was charged to her online bank account at a gas station in a city she has never visited. Which of the following should she do first:

options.A: Contact his bank to report the charge
options.B: Wait until his next statement arrives
options.C: Post about the charge on social media
options.D: Ignore it because it might be a mistake

questions.explanation: Contact his bank to report the charge. An unfamiliar charge may be fraud, so Simone should contact her bank right away using the number on her card or the bank's official app, not a number in a text that could be a scam. Quick reporting helps her recover the money and block further charges. Ignoring it or waiting for her next statement gives criminals more time, and posting on social media doesn't solve the problem. Account alerts are one of the easiest tools for catching fraud early, so it's worth turning them on for every account.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage online accounts

questions.question: A coworker asks Jalen to clock in for her because she'll be 20 minutes late. It is the third time this month she has asked. She says, "Everyone does it, and the manager will never know." What should Jalen do?

options.A: Clock her in and tell no one
options.B: Politely refuse and suggest she call the manager
options.C: Clock her in this one time only
options.D: Report her without saying anything to her first

questions.explanation: Politely refuse and suggest she call the manager. Clocking in for someone else is time theft and violates company policy, even if others do it. Jalen should politely refuse and suggest she call the manager to explain she'll be late. Doing it once or secretly still makes him part of the dishonesty, and the claim that everyone does it doesn't make it right. Reporting her immediately without talking to her may be appropriate if the behavior continues, but a direct, honest refusal first often resolves the situation.

performanceIndicator.text: Recognize and respond to ethical dilemmas

questions.question: Governments create import and export laws mainly to

options.B: protect security and domestic jobs.
options.C: set the prices of every product.
options.D: stop all trade with other countries.

questions.explanation: Protect security and domestic jobs. Import and export laws control what goods can enter or leave a country. They help protect national security, for example by limiting exports of military technology, and they can protect domestic industries and consumers through tariffs, quotas and safety standards. These laws don't stop all trade, set every product's price or require businesses to export. Companies that trade internationally must understand these rules, because violations can lead to fines, seized shipments or loss of export privileges.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of import/export law

questions.question: A hotel is choosing between two laundry vendors with similar prices. Which of the following would best help the hotel decide:

options.A: Asking guests to vote on the vendor
options.B: Picking the vendor whose name sounds better
options.C: Choosing the vendor with the newest trucks

questions.explanation: Checking the vendors' references. References from other customers show how reliable each vendor really is, including whether deliveries arrive on time and linens come back clean. When prices are similar, reliability and quality often decide the best choice. New trucks don't guarantee good service, a vendor's name says nothing about quality, and guests don't have the information needed to choose a laundry vendor. Many businesses also try a vendor for a short trial period before signing a long contract.

performanceIndicator.text: Select vendors

questions.question: A young adult who drives to work most likely needs which type of insurance by law in most states?

options.B: Pet health insurance
options.C: Auto liability insurance

questions.explanation: Auto liability insurance. Nearly every state requires drivers to carry auto liability insurance, which pays for injuries or damage the driver causes to others. Life insurance protects dependents if the insured person dies, pet insurance covers veterinary bills, and travel insurance covers trip problems such as cancellations. None of these is legally required for driving. Determining insurance needs means considering legal requirements, what one owns, who depends on one's income and what risks one can afford to cover alone.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine insurance needs

questions.question: An employee who questions an outdated procedure and suggests a better way to do it is

options.B: avoiding responsibility.
options.C: showing poor teamwork.

questions.explanation: Challenging the status quo. Challenging the status quo means questioning "the way things have always been done" and suggesting improvements. Doing so respectfully, with a better idea, helps organizations grow and stay competitive. Suggesting improvements isn't the same as refusing to follow rules, since the employee can follow the current procedure while proposing a change. It shows good teamwork and responsibility rather than avoiding them. Many companies encourage employees to challenge outdated practices because they see problems firsthand.

performanceIndicator.text: Challenge the status quo

questions.question: A sales manager who shares stories about how the team's work helps local families buy their first homes is mainly trying to

options.B: avoid setting goals for the team.
options.C: inspire a sense of purpose.

questions.explanation: Inspire a sense of purpose. Inspiring leaders help people see the meaning in their work, which motivates them more than orders or rewards alone. Stories about families buying first homes connect the team's daily tasks to real impact. The stories don't reduce commissions, replace training or remove the need for goals; inspiration works alongside these. Leaders also inspire by setting a positive example, expressing confidence in their teams and celebrating progress, which helps employees stay committed when the work is difficult.

performanceIndicator.text: Inspire others

questions.question: A hotel sales coordinator learns that the head chef strongly influences which events the hotel accepts. Which of the following is the best way for her to work with this political relationship:

options.B: Spread rumors to reduce the chef's influence
options.C: Build a respectful relationship with the chef
options.D: Ignore the chef and go straight to the CEO

questions.explanation: Build a respectful relationship with the chef. Building a respectful working relationship with the chef, such as asking for input early on menus for proposed events, can help her ideas gain support. Going around the chef to the CEO may damage trust, spreading rumors is unethical and harmful, and refusing to propose events keeps her from doing her job. Understanding and working positively with informal influence is a valuable skill, because many decisions in organizations depend on relationships as well as formal authority.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of political relationships within an organization

questions.question: A bakery owner chooses a reliable, slightly more expensive supplier because she wants customers to keep trusting her quality for years. She is

options.A: focusing only on what benefits oneself today.
options.B: ignoring how customers might be affected.
options.C: weighing how choices affect others later.

questions.explanation: Weighing how choices affect others later. Assessing long-term impact means looking beyond immediate results to consider how a decision will affect customers, coworkers, the community and the business over time. A choice that helps today might cause harm later, such as a pushy sale that loses a customer's trust. Focusing only on oneself, ignoring customers and making quick decisions without thinking all skip this important step. People who consider long-term impact tend to build stronger relationships and reputations. Asking "Who will this affect next year?" is a simple way to practice this habit.

performanceIndicator.text: Assess long-term value and impact of actions on others

questions.question: When a company's research shows that a product works for only some users, providing information ethically means

options.B: using fake customer reviews.
options.C: hiding the research results.

questions.explanation: Describing its results honestly. Ethical information is accurate and complete enough for customers to make informed decisions. If a product works for only some users, the company should describe its results honestly rather than exaggerating them. Claiming it works for everyone is misleading, hiding the research keeps customers uninformed, and fake reviews are deceptive and illegal. Honest claims may produce fewer sales at first, but they protect the company from lawsuits and help build long-term trust with customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ethical considerations in providing information

questions.question: Rules created by government agencies, such as workplace safety rules from OSHA, are part of

options.B: administrative law.
options.C: criminal law.

questions.explanation: Administrative law. Administrative law includes the rules and regulations that government agencies create and enforce under authority given to them by Congress or state legislatures. OSHA's safety rules, the FTC's advertising rules and the EPA's pollution rules are examples. Constitutional law comes from the Constitution, criminal law deals with crimes against society, and contract law governs agreements between parties. Businesses must follow administrative rules carefully, because agencies can investigate, issue fines and require changes. Agencies usually publish proposed rules and ask the public for comments before finalizing them.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of administrative law

questions.question: Marcus sees a document on the printer showing that a coworker is being considered for a promotion. Later, a teammate asks Marcus if he has heard anything about promotions. What should he do?

options.B: Post the news in a group chat
options.C: Share the details he saw

questions.explanation: Keep the information private. The promotion is confidential and not yet decided, so sharing it could embarrass the coworker, create tension and violate company policy. Marcus should keep the information private and could quietly return the document to its owner or HR. Sharing details, hinting that he knows something and posting in a group chat all break confidentiality. Employees who handle sensitive information responsibly earn trust, which often leads to more responsibility and opportunities over time. Keeping confidences is one of the fastest ways to earn a reputation for trustworthiness.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain the confidentiality of others

questions.question: A manager can best foster open, honest communication on a team by

options.B: thanking people who share bad news.
options.C: keeping all decisions secret.

questions.explanation: Thanking people who share bad news. When managers respond to bad news with appreciation rather than anger, employees feel safe speaking up early, which helps the team fix problems before they grow. Punishing disagreement, keeping decisions secret and interrupting concerns all teach employees to stay quiet. Other ways to encourage open communication include asking for feedback, admitting one's own mistakes and following up on concerns. Teams that communicate openly usually make better decisions because they hear about problems sooner. Leaders who listen calmly to problems are often the first to hear about opportunities, too.

performanceIndicator.text: Foster open, honest communication

questions.question: A helpful first step when facing an ethical dilemma at work is to

options.A: ignore the problem until it disappears.
options.B: ask what will benefit you most.
options.C: do whatever is fastest.
options.D: identify the issue and who is affected.

questions.explanation: Identify the issue and who is affected. Clearly identifying the ethical issue and who could be affected, such as customers, coworkers or the company, helps a person think through the consequences of each choice. Next steps often include considering company policies, laws and personal values, and seeking advice if needed. Doing what is fastest, choosing what benefits oneself most and ignoring the problem can lead to poor decisions. Many companies provide ethics hotlines or advisors for employees who need help with difficult situations.

performanceIndicator.text: Recognize and respond to ethical dilemmas

questions.question: Ethics are best described as

options.A: laws passed by the federal government only.
options.B: personal preferences about food and music.
options.C: standards for deciding what is right or wrong.
options.D: rules that apply only to large companies.

questions.explanation: Standards for deciding what is right or wrong. Ethics are principles or standards that guide people in deciding what is right or wrong, such as honesty, fairness and respect. Laws often reflect ethical values, but ethics go further: an action can be legal yet still unethical, such as breaking a promise. Ethics apply to individuals and organizations of all sizes, not only large companies, and they concern right and wrong rather than personal tastes. Businesses with strong ethical standards tend to earn more trust from customers and employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of ethics

questions.question: Before analyzing sales data, an analyst should check it for errors and missing values. This step is important mainly because

options.B: analysts are paid by the hour.
options.C: clean data is always more expensive.
options.D: bad data leads to wrong conclusions.

questions.explanation: Bad data leads to wrong conclusions. Data analysis is only as reliable as the data behind it. Errors, duplicates and missing values can distort averages, trends and comparisons, leading managers to make poor decisions. Cleaning data doesn't make it more expensive, the reason has nothing to do with how analysts are paid, and errors make results less accurate rather than better. Data cleaning is often the most time-consuming part of analysis, but skipping it can make an entire report misleading.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the principles of data analysis

questions.question: When selecting a new vendor, a restaurant should first

options.A: pick the vendor its competitor uses.
options.B: choose the vendor with the biggest ads.
options.C: sign a contract with the first caller.
options.D: identify exactly what it needs to buy.

questions.explanation: Identify exactly what it needs to buy. Vendor selection starts by defining needs, such as the products, quantities, quality standards, delivery schedule and budget. With those needs clear, the restaurant can compare vendors fairly. Choosing based on advertising, signing with the first caller or copying a competitor skips the evaluation process and may lead to a poor fit. After defining needs, buyers usually request quotes, check references and compare price, quality and reliability before choosing a vendor. Writing needs down also makes it easier to compare vendors' quotes fairly.

performanceIndicator.text: Select vendors

questions.question: Tasha, 32, is married and has two young children who depend on her income. She already has health insurance through her employer and auto insurance for her car. Which type of insurance would best protect her family if she died unexpectedly?

options.B: Renters insurance
options.C: Life insurance

questions.explanation: Life insurance. Life insurance pays a benefit to beneficiaries, such as Tasha's spouse and children, if she dies, helping them replace her income and cover expenses like housing and education. Renters insurance protects belongings in a rented home, pet insurance covers veterinary costs, and travel insurance covers trip-related problems. People with dependents often need life insurance most, and many financial advisors suggest coverage equal to several years of income. Term life insurance is often an affordable option for young families.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine insurance needs

questions.question: Keon leads a five-person design team and learns that a client project went over budget weeks ago, but no one told him. Which action would best encourage the team to share problems sooner?

options.A: Review results only once a year
options.B: Criticize anyone who points out problems
options.C: Tell the team the project can't fail

questions.explanation: Invite concerns without blame. Asking for concerns directly, and responding calmly and without blame, shows the team it is safe to be honest. Over time, team members will share problems earlier, which saves time and money. Criticizing those who point out problems teaches people to stay silent, claiming the project can't fail discourages honest discussion, and yearly reviews come too late to fix a struggling project. Regular check-ins with simple questions, such as "What's not working?" help build this habit.

performanceIndicator.text: Foster open, honest communication

questions.question: Raj's personal balance sheet shows a car worth $8,000, savings of $2,500 and $1,000 in checking. It also shows a car loan balance of $5,500 and a credit card balance of $500. What is Raj's net worth?
questions.explanation: $5,500. Raj's assets total $8,000 + $2,500 + $1,000 = $11,500, and his liabilities total $5,500 + $500 = $6,000. Net worth equals assets minus liabilities: $11,500 - $6,000 = $5,500. The answer $11,500 is his total assets, $6,000 is his total liabilities, and $17,500 adds assets and liabilities instead of subtracting. A positive net worth means he owns more than he owes, and paying down the car loan will increase it over time. Lenders also review net worth when deciding whether to approve some loans. Lenders also review net worth when deciding whether to approve some loans.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine personal net worth

questions.question: A sales team is told that anyone who misses this month's quota may lose a bonus. Which of the following is most likely to create ethical dilemmas for team members:

options.A: Pressure to meet goals or deadlines
options.B: Working in a well-lit office
options.C: Having too few coworkers to talk to

questions.explanation: Pressure to meet goals or deadlines. Pressure to meet sales goals, deadlines or budgets can tempt employees to cut corners, such as exaggerating a product's benefits or skipping required steps. This pressure is one of the most common sources of ethical dilemmas. The number of coworkers, office lighting and using a company computer don't by themselves create ethical conflicts. Companies can reduce these dilemmas by setting realistic goals, providing clear ethics policies and making it easy for employees to ask for guidance.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain reasons for ethical dilemmas

questions.question: Jada manages social media for a bookstore and also has a personal account. After a frustrating day, she wants to post a complaint about a rude customer. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice:

options.A: Avoid posting about the customer anywhere
options.B: Post it on the store's account
options.C: Ask followers to guess who the customer is
options.D: Post it on her personal account with the customer's name

questions.explanation: Avoid posting about the customer anywhere. Posting about a customer, even on a personal account, could embarrass the customer, violate privacy and reflect poorly on the store if people know where Jada works. The most appropriate choice is not to post about the customer at all. Posting on the store's account is clearly unprofessional, naming the customer on her personal account is worse, and asking followers to guess still invites gossip. Separating business and personal social media, and keeping work complaints offline, protects both Jada and her employer.

performanceIndicator.text: Distinguish between using social media for business and personal purposes

questions.question: A good practice for managing online financial accounts is to

options.B: share login details with friends.
options.C: log in on public computers often.

questions.explanation: Use two-factor authentication. Two-factor authentication requires a second step, such as a code sent to a phone, which makes it much harder for someone to break into an account even with a stolen password. Using the same password everywhere means one breach can expose every account, sharing logins gives others access to one's money, and public computers may record login information. Other good habits include checking accounts regularly, turning on alerts and logging out after each session.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage online accounts

questions.question: A new employee notices that one senior coworker strongly influences which ideas the manager accepts. Understanding this is part of recognizing

options.B: the company's pricing strategy.
options.C: its political relationships.

questions.explanation: Its political relationships. Political relationships are the informal patterns of influence and alliances within an organization, which may differ from the official organizational chart. Knowing that a senior coworker influences decisions helps the new employee understand how ideas get approved and whose support may be helpful. The official chart shows formal reporting lines, pricing strategy concerns product prices, and safety rules protect employees. Understanding political relationships can help employees work effectively without engaging in manipulation. Observing how decisions are actually made is part of learning a new workplace.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of political relationships within an organization

questions.question: A person's net worth is calculated by

options.B: subtracting liabilities from assets.
options.C: subtracting expenses from income.

questions.explanation: Subtracting liabilities from assets. Net worth equals total assets, such as cash, savings and the value of a car, minus total liabilities, such as loans and credit card balances. It shows what a person would have left if he or she sold everything and paid all debts. Adding income and expenses, or subtracting expenses from income, describes a budget's cash flow, not net worth, and adding assets and liabilities produces a meaningless number. Tracking net worth over time shows whether a person's financial position is improving.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine personal net worth

questions.question: Devon is comparing two furniture-store payment plans. To find the total cost of credit for each plan, he should add up

options.B: the store's advertising costs.
options.C: interest and any fees charged.

questions.explanation: Interest and any fees charged. The cost of credit is the extra amount a borrower pays beyond the amount borrowed, including interest and fees such as processing, annual or late fees. The amount borrowed is the principal, which is repaid but isn't a cost of credit. The borrower's income affects whether he or she qualifies but isn't part of the cost, and a store's advertising costs aren't charged as credit costs. Comparing the total cost of credit helps borrowers choose the cheapest loan or card.

performanceIndicator.text: Calculate the cost of credit

questions.question: A company advertises that its juice is "packed with vitamins," which is true, but leaves out that each bottle contains 40 grams of sugar. Which of the following statements best fits this situation:

options.A: Legal actions can still be unethical
options.B: Ethics and laws are exactly the same
options.C: Anything legal is always ethical

questions.explanation: Legal actions can still be unethical. Laws set minimum standards society enforces, while ethics involve broader judgments about right and wrong. An action, such as making a misleading but technically true claim, can be legal yet unethical. Saying anything legal is ethical ignores this gap, ethics and laws overlap but aren't identical, and many laws, such as those against fraud, are based on ethical values. Ethical businesses aim higher than the legal minimum, which helps them avoid harming customers and damaging their reputations.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of ethics

questions.question: Research for a coffee shop finds that afternoon sales are low because nearby office workers don't know the shop offers fast lunch items. Which recommendation is most actionable?

options.A: Note that afternoon sales are low
options.B: Stop selling lunch items
options.C: Promote lunch to nearby offices
options.D: Raise prices on all lunch items

questions.explanation: Promote lunch to nearby offices. The research identifies a specific cause, low awareness among office workers, so promoting lunch items to nearby offices, for example with flyers or a lunch-delivery offer, addresses it directly. The shop can track whether afternoon sales rise. Simply noting that sales are low repeats the finding, raising prices doesn't fix the awareness problem, and stopping lunch sales gives up a possible source of revenue. Strong recommendations connect clearly to the cause the research uncovered.

performanceIndicator.text: Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations

questions.question: A clothing retailer's CRM system notices that a loyal customer hasn't purchased anything in six months and automatically emails her a personalized offer. Which of the following is the main purpose of this technology:

options.B: Keeping the customer relationship active
options.C: Replacing all store employees

questions.explanation: Keeping the customer relationship active. CRM technology tracks customer behavior and can trigger personalized messages, such as a special offer when a regular customer stops shopping. The goal is to remind her of the store and encourage her to return, which keeps the relationship active. The system isn't meant to charge higher prices, delete her records or replace employees. Companies must use customer data responsibly and follow privacy rules, but when used well, CRM tools help businesses keep customers longer.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management

questions.question: Surveys show that many of a hardware store's regular buyers would order supplies online for curbside pickup if they could. The most actionable recommendation is to

options.B: close the physical store immediately.
options.C: say that customers seem interested.

questions.explanation: Test an online store. Actionable recommendations turn research findings into specific steps that a business can carry out and measure. Launching a simple online store and tracking sales responds directly to the finding and lets the business learn whether online shopping pays off. Saying customers seem interested restates the finding without an action, ignoring the research wastes it, and closing the physical store overreacts, since many customers still prefer shopping in person. Good recommendations are specific, realistic and tied to the data.

performanceIndicator.text: Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations

questions.question: An online retailer's data-mining software predicts that certain customers are experiencing financial hardship based on their purchases, and the marketing team wants to target them with high-interest credit offers. Which of the following best describes the ethical concern:

options.A: It costs too much to send emails
options.B: It exploits vulnerable people
options.C: It uses data that is too old

questions.explanation: It exploits vulnerable people. Using data mining to identify financially stressed customers and push high-interest credit offers could take advantage of people in a vulnerable situation, encouraging debt they can't afford. Even if legal, it raises serious ethical concerns. The age of the data and the cost of emails aren't the main issues, and the plan is unlikely to help customers save money. Ethical data mining considers how predictions will be used and whether the results could harm the people behind the data.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of ethics in data mining

questions.question: An analyst finds that customers who buy umbrellas also tend to buy rain boots. Which of the following conclusions is most appropriate:

options.A: The products are often bought together
options.B: Umbrellas cause people to buy boots
options.C: The data must be wrong
options.D: Rain boots should be removed from stores

questions.explanation: The products are often bought together. The data shows a correlation, meaning the two products tend to be purchased together, likely because both are useful in rainy weather. It doesn't prove that buying an umbrella causes someone to buy boots. Removing rain boots would ignore a useful sales pattern, and there is no reason to assume the data is wrong. A store might use this finding to display umbrellas and boots near each other or offer them in a bundle.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the principles of data analysis

questions.question: A receptionist at a medical office maintains the confidentiality of others by making a habit of

options.B: reading others' email when curious.
options.C: telling coworkers about others' personal problems.
options.D: not sharing private information without permission.

questions.explanation: Not sharing private information without permission. Confidentiality means keeping private information, such as a coworker's health issue or a customer's account details, to oneself unless one has permission or a legitimate business reason to share it. Telling coworkers about others' problems, posting company information online and reading others' email all violate confidentiality. Many jobs require employees to sign confidentiality agreements. Respecting confidentiality builds trust and may also be required by privacy laws, especially in health care and finance. Locking screens and storing files securely also protect confidential information.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain the confidentiality of others

questions.question: A customer who travels often for work asks a salesperson whether a laptop's battery lasts 12 hours, as an online ad claims. The salesperson knows that in normal use it lasts closer to 7 hours. What is the most ethical response?

options.B: Explain that it's about 7 hours
options.C: Change the subject to avoid the question
options.D: Confirm that it lasts a full 12 hours

questions.explanation: Explain that it's about 7 hours. Providing information ethically means being honest, even when the answer might cost a sale. The salesperson should explain that typical battery life is about 7 hours and perhaps note what conditions could make it last longer. Confirming the 12-hour claim would mislead the customer, changing the subject avoids honesty, and saying battery life doesn't matter dismisses an important concern. Honest answers build trust, and customers who feel misled often return products and leave negative reviews.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ethical considerations in providing information

questions.question: The Federal Trade Commission issues a rule requiring companies to clearly disclose when online reviews are paid for. Which of the following best describes how this affects businesses:

options.A: It replaces all other advertising laws
options.B: They can ignore it because Congress didn't write it
options.C: They must follow the agency's rule or face penalties
options.D: It applies only to government websites

questions.explanation: They must follow the agency's rule or face penalties. Agency rules, part of administrative law, have the force of law when agencies create them under authority granted by Congress. Businesses must follow the FTC's disclosure rule or risk investigations, fines and orders to change their practices. They can't ignore it because Congress didn't write it directly, it applies to businesses that use paid reviews, not just government websites, and it adds to rather than replaces other advertising laws. Many companies have legal teams that track new agency rules.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of administrative law

questions.question: Diego runs the official social media account for a bike shop. Which of the following would be appropriate for him to post there:

options.A: An announcement of a new product
options.B: A complaint about a coworker
options.C: An employee's personal political opinions

questions.explanation: An announcement of a new product. Business social media accounts represent the company, so posts should support its goals, such as announcing products, sharing events or answering customer questions. An employee's personal political opinions can offend customers and don't represent the company, private customer details violate privacy, and complaints about coworkers are unprofessional. Many companies have social media policies that explain what may be posted and who is allowed to post on business accounts. Separate accounts make it easier to keep personal opinions away from the business. Employees should also follow their company's social media policy.

performanceIndicator.text: Distinguish between using social media for business and personal purposes

questions.question: A sporting goods chain plans to analyze ten years of loyalty-card purchases to find new sales opportunities. Which of the following is the most important ethical consideration:

options.A: Selling customers' data without telling them
options.B: Using data only as customers were told
options.C: Sharing the data with any company that asks
options.D: Collecting more data without any limits

questions.explanation: Using data only as customers were told. Data mining can reveal useful patterns, but ethical use means respecting customers' privacy and using data only in ways the company disclosed in its privacy policy. Sharing data with any company, selling it without telling customers and collecting unlimited data all disregard customers' trust and may violate privacy laws. Companies should also protect data securely and avoid using it to make unfair or embarrassing predictions about individuals. Ethical practices help businesses keep customers' trust.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of ethics in data mining

questions.question: A company that uses a chatbot on its website to answer customers' common questions at any hour is using technology to

options.B: provide faster customer service.
options.C: avoid all contact with customers.
options.D: raise the price of its products.

questions.explanation: Provide faster customer service. Chatbots can answer routine questions, such as store hours or order status, instantly and around the clock, which improves convenience and frees employees to handle more complex issues. They don't eliminate customer contact, since customers should still be able to reach a person when needed. Chatbots don't raise prices or replace products. Customer relationship management technology works best when it makes service faster and more personal rather than more frustrating. Many companies review chatbot conversations to improve answers over time.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management

questions.question: A loan officer could approve a large loan that would earn him a bonus, but he believes the borrower likely can't afford the payments, since her income has dropped twice in the past year. Which of the following best reflects considering the long-term impact of his actions:

options.A: Approve it and hope the borrower manages
options.B: Decline the loan or suggest a smaller one
options.C: Approve the loan to earn his bonus
options.D: Tell the borrower to lie about her income

questions.explanation: Decline the loan or suggest a smaller one. Approving a loan the borrower can't afford could lead to missed payments, damaged credit and financial stress for her, as well as losses for the bank. Declining it or suggesting a more affordable amount protects both. Approving it for the bonus or hoping she manages ignores the likely harm, and encouraging her to lie about income is fraud. Thinking about how decisions will affect people months or years later is a key part of ethical decision making in finance.

performanceIndicator.text: Assess long-term value and impact of actions on others

questions.question: A U.S. company wants to sell advanced encryption software to customers in another country. Before shipping, the company learns it needs a government document approving the sale. This document is a(n)

options.B: import quota.
options.C: trademark registration.

questions.explanation: Export license. An export license is government permission to send certain goods or technology out of the country. Some products, such as advanced encryption software or military equipment, require licenses because of national security concerns. An import quota limits how much of a product can enter a country, a tax return reports income to the government, and a trademark registration protects a brand name. Exporting without a required license can lead to serious penalties, so companies check export rules before selling abroad.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of import/export law

questions.question: Two employees in the shipping department often complain about a new supervisor and try to get coworkers to sign a petition against her. Which response would best help a coworker handle this office politics?

options.B: Spread rumors about the two coworkers
options.C: Join the gossip to fit in with the group
options.D: Refuse to work with anyone on the team

questions.explanation: Stay respectful; avoid the gossip. Staying respectful and avoiding gossip lets the employee keep good relationships without being drawn into harmful behavior. If the gossip affects work, the employee can speak with a supervisor. Joining in can damage his reputation, spreading rumors about the two coworkers adds to the problem, and refusing to work with anyone hurts the team and his own performance. Handling office politics well often means focusing on the work and treating everyone fairly. Building good relationships with the new manager also helps protect against the gossip's effects.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of office politics

questions.question: Tomas takes a one-year, $2,000 loan at 6% simple interest from his credit union and pays a $40 application fee. What is his total cost of credit?
questions.explanation: $160. Interest equals $2,000 x 0.06 x 1 = $120. Adding the $40 application fee gives a total cost of credit of $120 + $40 = $160. The answer $120 includes only the interest, $40 includes only the fee, and $2,160 is the total amount Tomas will repay, including the $2,000 he borrowed. Lenders must disclose these costs under the Truth in Lending Act, so borrowers can compare offers using the annual percentage rate, which includes most fees.

performanceIndicator.text: Calculate the cost of credit

questions.question: The director of a community food bank wants volunteers to help collect 10,000 pounds of food during the holidays. Which approach would most likely inspire them?

options.A: Offer no updates during the food drive
options.B: Keep the goal secret until it is reached
options.C: Tell volunteers the goal is mandatory
options.D: Share how many families the food will feed

questions.explanation: Share how many families the food will feed. Inspiration comes from helping people understand why a goal matters. Sharing how many families the food will feed turns a number into a meaningful purpose that volunteers care about. Calling the goal mandatory can feel like pressure, especially for volunteers, keeping it secret makes it impossible to work toward, and offering no updates leaves people unsure whether their effort is making a difference. Regular progress updates and thanking volunteers publicly also keep energy high throughout the drive.

performanceIndicator.text: Inspire others

questions.question: For years, a bank has required customers to visit a branch to update their mailing addresses. A teller suggests letting customers update addresses securely online. Which of the following best describes the teller's suggestion:

options.B: Ignoring security requirements
options.C: Creating more work for customers

questions.explanation: Constructively questioning a habit. The teller is questioning a long-standing practice and proposing a change that would save customers trips to the branch. That is challenging the status quo in a constructive way. Making a suggestion isn't breaking rules, the idea reduces rather than increases customers' work, and the suggestion specifically includes secure online updates, so it doesn't ignore security. Leaders can encourage this kind of thinking by inviting suggestions and explaining why ideas are or aren't adopted.

performanceIndicator.text: Challenge the status quo
